{{AFC comment|1=Note: This draft started from a complete copy of [[Onmyōji]] as it has a lot of redlinks with claims I want to keep. I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}} {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=draft}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>
The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|12=draft}} within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=draft}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=draft}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=draft}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=draft}}, individuals of higher ranks, such as the fifth or sixth ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=draft}}).
The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=draft}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=draft}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=draft}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the {{ill|bells|ja|鐘|12=draft}} located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=draft}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.
In {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|12=draft}}, a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=draft}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=draft}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>
The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the {{ill|Insei|ja|院政|12=draft}} period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=draft}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=draft}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=draft}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=draft}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|12=draft}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|ja|出羽国|12=draft}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.
== History == Later, [[Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=draft}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=draft}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=draft}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}}
{{AFC comment|1=Note: This draft started from a complete copy of [[Onmyōji]] as it has a lot of redlinks with claims I want to keep. I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}} {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=draft}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>
The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=draft}} under the {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|12=draft}} within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=draft}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=draft}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=draft}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=draft}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=draft}}, individuals of higher ranks, such as the fifth or sixth ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=draft}}).
The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=draft}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=draft}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=draft}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the {{ill|bells|ja|鐘|12=draft}} located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=draft}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.
In {{ill|Tang dynasty|ja|唐|12=draft}}, a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=draft}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=draft}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>
The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the {{ill|Insei|ja|院政|12=draft}} period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=draft}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=draft}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=draft}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=draft}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=draft}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu|ja|大宰府|12=draft}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|ja|Mutsu Province|12=draft}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|ja|出羽国|12=draft}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.
== History == Later, [[Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=draft}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=draft}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=draft}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=draft}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].
== Related Articles == * {{ill|Ritsuryō system|ja|律令制|12=draft}} * {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=draft}} * {{ill|Water clock|ja|漏刻|12=draft}}

'''漏刻博士'''（ろうこくはかせ）は、[[日本]][[律令制]]において[[陰陽寮]]に置かれた[[博士 (文官)|博士]]。[[和訓]]は「ときつかさ」。[[唐名]]は司辰・契壷司。定員2名で時には[[権官]]が置かれた。[[従七位下]]相当であるが、五位・六位が任じられた例もある（『[[職源鈔]]』）。
[[仕丁]]から選抜された[[守辰丁]]（20名）を率いて[[漏刻]]を警備するとともに、時刻を計り、定時に守辰丁に命じて陰陽寮内に設置された[[鐘]]を打たせた。[[天皇]]の[[行幸]]の際には漏刻博士1名と守辰丁12名が漏刻とともに随従する義務があった。
なお、唐にも漏刻博士の[[官職]]は存在したが、唐では漏刻の実務は挈壺正・司辰・漏刻典事が行って漏刻博士は漏刻生を教育することが職掌とされていた。これに対して、日本では挈壺正・司辰・漏刻典事が設けられずに漏刻博士がその職掌を行い、反対に漏刻生の制度も設けられなかったために漏刻博士に教育の職掌が無かった（これは実務を行いながら、学生の教育も行った[[天文博士]]、[[暦博士]]と異なる）<ref>木下正史『古代の漏刻と時刻制度』（吉川弘文館、2020年）ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2 P307-312.</ref>。
もっとも、漏刻の技術は比較的早くに途絶えたとされ、[[院政]]期には[[賀茂朝臣氏]]・[[阿倍氏|安倍氏]]の一員やその推挙する門人のための官職となる。[[菅野季親]]・[[菅野季長|季長]]は漏刻ではなく、[[年筮]]の達人として漏刻博士となったとされる。なお、[[大宰府]]・[[陸奥国]]（後に[[出羽国]]を追加）にも漏刻は設置されたが、博士は置かれずに守辰丁が管理していたとされている。
なお、[[朝鮮]]でも『[[三国史記]]』には[[新羅]]が漏刻博士を置いたことが記されている。

I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|qq=|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|qq=|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|qq=|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|qq=|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|qq=|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|qq=|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

{{AfC comment|1=Note: This draft started from a complete copy of [[Onmyōji]] as it has a lot of redlinks with claims I want to keep. I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy.
