I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the [[:en:Ministry of the Center|Ministry of the Center]] the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the [[:en:Ritsuryō|Ritsuryō system]] within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the [[:en:Bell|bells]] located within the Onmyōryō. During the [[:en:Emperor of Japan|Emperor]]'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In [[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang dynasty]], a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the [[:en:Cloistered rule|Insei]] period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in [[:en:Dazaifu (government)|Dazaifu]] and [[:en:Mutsu Province|Mutsu Province]] (and later in [[:en:Dewa Province|Dewa Province]]), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, [[:en:Emperor Tenmu|Emperor Tenmu]] was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the [[:en:Jinshin War|Jinshin War]]. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first [[:en:Observatory|Observatory]] in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the [[:en:Yōrō Code|Yōrō Code]] established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the [[:en:Turtle shell|Turtle shell]] diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|WD=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center}} the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|WD=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}} within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the {{ill|Bell|en|Bell|WD=Q101401|lt=bells}} located within the Onmyōryō. During the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=Emperor}}'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In {{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang dynasty}}, a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Insei}} period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|WD=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|en|Dewa Province|WD=Q876032|lt=Dewa Province}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|WD=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the {{ill|Jinshin War|en|Jinshin War|WD=Q2378252|lt=Jinshin War}}. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first {{ill|Observatory|en|Observatory|WD=Q62832|lt=Observatory}} in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|WD=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center}} the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|WD=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}} within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the {{ill|Bell|en|Bell|WD=Q101401|lt=bells}} located within the Onmyōryō. During the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=Emperor}}'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In {{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang dynasty}}, a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Insei}} period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|WD=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|en|Dewa Province|WD=Q876032|lt=Dewa Province}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|WD=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the {{ill|Jinshin War|en|Jinshin War|WD=Q2378252|lt=Jinshin War}}. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first {{ill|Observatory|en|Observatory|WD=Q62832|lt=Observatory}} in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the {{ill|Yōrō Code|en|Yōrō Code|WD=Q2575743|lt=Yōrō Code}} established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the {{ill|Turtle shell|en|Turtle shell|WD=Q13486671|lt=Turtle shell}} diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

I will trim down into just the claim on an individual thing later[[User:Immanuelle|'''Immanuel'''le]] ❤️💚💙 [[User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)]] 01:41, 25 April 2023 (UTC)}}

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|WD=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center}} the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|WD=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}} within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the {{ill|Bell|en|Bell|WD=Q101401|lt=bells}} located within the Onmyōryō. During the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=Emperor}}'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In {{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang dynasty}}, a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Insei}} period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|WD=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|en|Dewa Province|WD=Q876032|lt=Dewa Province}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|WD=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the {{ill|Jinshin War|en|Jinshin War|WD=Q2378252|lt=Jinshin War}}. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first {{ill|Observatory|en|Observatory|WD=Q62832|lt=Observatory}} in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the {{ill|Yōrō Code|en|Yōrō Code|WD=Q2575743|lt=Yōrō Code}} established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the {{ill|Turtle shell|en|Turtle shell|WD=Q13486671|lt=Turtle shell}} diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|WD=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center}} the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|WD=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}} within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the {{ill|Bell|en|Bell|WD=Q101401|lt=bells}} located within the Onmyōryō. During the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=Emperor}}'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In {{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang dynasty}}, a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Insei}} period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|WD=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|en|Dewa Province|WD=Q876032|lt=Dewa Province}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|WD=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the {{ill|Jinshin War|en|Jinshin War|WD=Q2378252|lt=Jinshin War}}. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first {{ill|Observatory|en|Observatory|WD=Q62832|lt=Observatory}} in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the {{ill|Yōrō Code|en|Yōrō Code|WD=Q2575743|lt=Yōrō Code}} established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the {{ill|Turtle shell|en|Turtle shell|WD=Q13486671|lt=Turtle shell}} diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|WD=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|en|Dewa Province|WD=Q876032|lt=Dewa Province}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|WD=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the {{ill|Jinshin War|en|Jinshin War|WD=Q2378252|lt=Jinshin War}}. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first {{ill|Observatory|en|Observatory|WD=Q62832|lt=Observatory}} in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the {{ill|Yōrō Code|en|Yōrō Code|WD=Q2575743|lt=Yōrō Code}} established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the {{ill|Turtle shell|en|Turtle shell|WD=Q13486671|lt=Turtle shell}} diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].

{{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} (Rōkoku Hakase, 漏刻博士) is position in the {{ill|Ministry of the Center|en|Ministry of the Center|WD=Q6867690|lt=Ministry of the Center}} the chief timekeeper.<ref name="titsingh427">Titsingh, Isaac. (1834). {{Google books|18oNAAAAIAAJ|''Annales des empereurs du japon,'' p. 427.|page=427}}</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/d8-3zya-0s65/download</ref><ref>https://academiccommons.columbia.edu/doi/10.7916/D8HD82PN/download</ref><ref>https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=8943</ref><ref>https://bazhum.muzhp.pl/media/files/Analecta_Nipponica/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202/Analecta_Nipponica-r2011-t1-s139-202.pdf</ref>

The position was a {{ill|Hakase|ja|博士 (文官)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakase|1=boshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q80995933}} under the {{ill|Ritsuryō|en|Ritsuryō|WD=Q742460|lt=Ritsuryō system}} within the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮|1=Yin-Yang Bureau|2=ja|3=陰陽寮|4=fr|5=Bureau d'Onmyō|6=zh|7=阴阳寮|8=ko|9=음양료|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyōryō|13=User:Immanuelle/Yin-Yang Bureau|qq=}}. The {{ill|Japanese reading|ja|和訓|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese reading|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 訓読み|1=kun'yomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1147749}} (和訓) for this position was "Tokitsukasa" (ときつかさ), while its {{ill|Chinese name|ja|唐名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chinese name|1=Chinese-style name|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q10922605}} was "Shijin" (司辰) or "Keiko-shi" (契壷司). Two individuals typically filled this role, though additional deputy officials ({{ill|Gonkan|ja|権官|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gonkan|qq=}}) were occasionally appointed. Officially classified as {{ill|Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|ja|従七位下|1=Junior Seventh Rank|lt=Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|3=従七位|1=Junior Seventh Rank|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank, Lower Grade|13=User:Immanuelle/Junior Seventh Rank|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 従七位}}, individuals of higher Ranks, such as the fifth or sixth Ranks, were sometimes appointed to this position (as noted in the {{ill|Shokugenshō|ja|職源鈔|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shokugenshō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}).

The Rōkoku Hakase supervised the {{ill|Morishin-chō|ja|守辰丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Morishin-chō|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, a group of 20 individuals selected from {{ill|Shichō|ja|仕丁|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shichō|1=Shichō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q109361855}}, who guarded the {{ill|Water clocks|ja|漏刻|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Water clocks|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 水時計|1=water clock|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q194173}} and operated them to measure time. At designated times, they would order the Morishin-chō to strike the {{ill|Bell|en|Bell|WD=Q101401|lt=bells}} located within the Onmyōryō. During the {{ill|Emperor of Japan|en|Emperor of Japan|WD=Q208233|lt=Emperor}}'s {{ill|Imperial visits|ja|行幸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Imperial visits|qq=}}, one Rōkoku Hakase and twelve Morishin-chō were required to accompany the water clock.

In {{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang dynasty}}, a similar role for a Rōkoku Hakase existed, but the responsibilities were distinct. In Tang China, the practical tasks of water clocks were managed by officials such as Kekkosei (挈壺正), Shijin (司辰), and Rokoku Tenshi (漏刻典事), while the Rōkoku Hakase focused on teaching students of water clocks (Rokokusei). Conversely, in Japan, the practical roles of Kekkosei and related officials were incorporated into the duties of the Rōkoku Hakase. Japan did not establish a Rokokusei system, meaning that Rōkoku Hakase did not have educational duties. This contrasts with the roles of {{ill|Tenmon Hakase|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}} (Astronomy Doctor) and {{ill|Reki Hakase|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}} (Calendar Doctor), who both managed practical tasks and taught students.<ref>Masashi Kinoshita, ''Kodai no Rōkoku to Jikoku Seido'' (Ancient Water Clocks and Time Systems), Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2020, ISBN 978-4-642-04657-2, pp. 307–312.</ref>

The water clock system appears to have declined relatively early. By the {{ill|Cloistered rule|en|Cloistered rule|WD=Q865416|lt=Insei}} period, the role of Rōkoku Hakase became symbolic, primarily awarded to members of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamo clan|qq=}} or {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Abe clan|qq=}} or their recommended disciples. Figures such as {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季親|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and {{ill|Sugano no Suketaka|ja|菅野季長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugano no Suketaka|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} became Rōkoku Hakase not for expertise in water clocks but for their skill in annual divination ({{ill|Nensei|ja|年筮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nensei|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}). Although water clocks were also installed in {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|en|Dazaifu (government)|WD=Q144845|lt=Dazaifu}} and {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|WD=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} (and later in {{ill|Dewa Province|en|Dewa Province|WD=Q876032|lt=Dewa Province}}), they were managed solely by Morishin-chō without a corresponding Hakase.

== History ==
Later, {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|WD=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}} was such a master of astrology and fugue that he took his own divination tools and told fortunes during the {{ill|Jinshin War|en|Jinshin War|WD=Q2378252|lt=Jinshin War}}. He also had a deep knowledge of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy, which led to the establishment of the Bureau of Onmyō and Japan's first {{ill|Observatory|en|Observatory|WD=Q62832|lt=Observatory}} in 676, and the use of the term "onmyōji" in 685, which further increased the popularity of the yin-and-yang five phases philosophy. In 718, the {{ill|Yōrō Code|en|Yōrō Code|WD=Q2575743|lt=Yōrō Code}} established the Bureau of Onmyō as an internal department of the Ministry of Center, and when it was stipulated that the positions of {{ill|Temmon Hakase|lt=Doctor of Astrology|ja|天文博士|1=Tenmon Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Temmon Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenmon Hakase|qq=}}, {{ill|Onmyō Hakase|lt=Doctor of Onmyō|ja|陰陽博士|1=Onmyō Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Onmyō Hakase|qq=}}, onmyōji, {{ill|Reki Hakase|lt=Doctor of Calendar|ja|暦博士|1=Reki Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Reki Hakase|qq=}}, and {{ill|Rōkoku Hakase|lt=Doctor of Water Clock|ja|漏刻博士|1=Rōkoku Hakase|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|13=User:Immanuelle/Rōkoku Hakase|qq=}} should be permanently assigned as technical officers, the Bureau of Onmyō became officially in charge of divination along with the {{ill|Turtle shell|en|Turtle shell|WD=Q13486671|lt=Turtle shell}} diviners who belonged to the [[Department of Divinities]].
